rationale: Permanent regression guard: an HVAC quote must not acquire vehicle or mechanic vocabulary that was never in the customer's text.
regression_origin: TASK-012 — an AC/HVAC quote produced vehicle-oriented output: the old missing_vehicle_context marker was set true on a non-vehicle quote, and the disclaimer named a mechanic. QC-1B replaced that field with the domain-neutral missing_quote_context, so this case guards the leakage behaviour rather than the deleted field name.
quote_text:
Northwind Climate Services - Service Estimate NW-2291

Unit: 1.5 ton split air conditioner (indoor + outdoor), installed 2019.
Customer complaint: reduced cooling over the last three weeks, outdoor unit running
continuously.

Technician findings on site visit: compressor drawing 14.2 A on start against a rated
8.6 A, suction line warm to touch, low-side pressure 42 psi against a specified 68-72 psi.
Soap test showed bubbling at the outdoor service valve joint.

Recommended work:
1. Compressor replacement (rotary, matched to unit tonnage), including brazing and full
   system evacuation.
2. Repair of the leaking service valve joint.
3. Refrigerant recharge to rated capacity after leak check is re-run.
4. Replacement of the filter drier (mandatory when the sealed system is opened).

Warranty on replaced compressor: 12 months from date of fitting, parts only. Labour on
any warranty claim is chargeable.
Work can be scheduled within 3 working days of approval.

should_identify: Compressor replacement is the major cost and the central recommendation.
The filter drier replacement is standard practice when a sealed refrigerant system is opened, not an add-on.
The warranty is parts-only, so a warranty claim would still incur labour charges.
should_preserve_uncertainty: The leak was located by soap test at one joint; whether that is the only leak is not established until the recharge leak check is re-run.
must_not_invent: Any vehicle, automotive, mechanic, brake, or tyre framing — this is a room air conditioner.
A verdict on whether replacing the compressor is better value than replacing the unit; the quote offers no basis for that comparison.
semantic_expectations.notes: Refrigerant handling and sealed-system work are technical and regulated, so recommending confirmation by a qualified HVAC technician is appropriate here — but the disclaimer must name an HVAC-appropriate professional, never a mechanic. Rubric dimension 6 covers whether the wording lands correctly; the deterministic check only proves vehicle words were not invented.
